name: Phase Sensitive Innovations
old_description: PHASE SENSITIVE INNOVATIONS (PSI) specializes in creating and incorporating photonic devices into various RF systems, including 5G wireless communication, high bandwidth RF-over-fiber, and antenna remoting.
about:
Phase Sensitive Innovations (PSI) is a small, high-technology company based in Newark, Delaware, specializing in RF photonic devices, components, and systems with a focus on the millimeter-wave region of the electromagnetic spectrum.

The company designs and manufactures high-speed UTC photodiodes, ultra-high-speed lithium niobate phase modulators (up to 500 GHz), broadband RF photonic links, and tunable optical paired source (TOPS) systems for wideband RF signal synthesis. It provides a full suite of photonic integrated circuit (PIC) capabilities — design, simulation, layout, multi-project wafer submission, and characterization — alongside custom RF design, RF component testing from DC to 1 THz, and RF/optical packaging (flip-chip, wire/ribbon bonding, hermetic sealing). In-house fabrication occupies over 3,000 sq ft of laboratory and cleanroom space, including a 1,200 sq ft ISO Class 6/7 cleanroom for wafer processing up to 6-inch diameter and 1,000+ sq ft for mid- and back-end assembly. The shop also runs a Mazak V500C CNC mill (3-axis and 3D simultaneous) and a 3NTR A2V4 3D printer for multi-material polymer parts.

PSI serves defense, industrial, 5G/6G cellular, radar, satellite, security, and communications markets. Its devices enable millimeter-wave imaging for security scanning and vision enhancement, RF-over-fiber links, antenna remoting, phased-array beamforming, and RF surveillance across microwave, millimeter-wave, and terahertz bands.

The company emphasizes its phase-locking upconversion technology, which it says delivers unprecedented beam-bandwidth processing for next-generation 5G and beyond. It also highlights photodiode power handling and linearity, lithium niobate modulators covering the full millimeter-wave spectrum, and an end-to-end PIC design-to-fabrication flow under an ISO 9001:2015 quality system certified by TÜV SÜD.

name: Piedmont Electrical Distributors of Greenville, Inc.
old_description: For over four decades, we’ve been the choice for quality electrical supplies and reliable service. Though we’ve grown, we remain a family-owned business in Greenville, SC. We’re dedicated to building strong relationships and providing the same personal service our customers have counted on since 1985.
about:
Piedmont Electrical Distributors of Greenville, Inc. was founded in 1985 in Greenville, South Carolina, by Tim Franke and his partner with the goal of becoming the electrical supplier for the region's construction and industrial markets. The business remains family-owned; Tim and his wife Francine led the company for years before their son Josh Franke took over as owner.

The company operates a 36,000-square-foot warehouse stocking a broad range of electrical products including circuit breakers, lighting fixtures, conduit, and wire. It serves customers across South Carolina, North Carolina, and Georgia through both delivery and a counter service for immediate pick-up. When items are not in stock, the team sources them quickly to minimize project downtime.

Piedmont Electrical primarily serves contractors and industrial facilities in the Upstate region. Its customer base includes on-site superintendents, electrical contractors, and industrial maintenance teams who rely on the distributor for timely material delivery and responsive communication. Testimonials from field supervisors highlight the company's willingness to deliver to job sites over an hour away and to accommodate last-minute order changes.

The company emphasizes its founding commitment to service and long-term relationships over transactional sales. It differentiates itself through fast delivery, reliable sourcing, and personable sales support, maintaining a team of outside and inside sales representatives, warehouse staff, and administrative personnel to keep projects moving.

about:
Pierce Manufacturing Company Inc. has operated in Kalispell, Montana since 1974. Founded as a small family-owned business, it remains under family ownership and serves the greater Flathead Valley area.

The company manufactures custom truck bodies and provides a full range of trailer repair and customization services. Its shop handles trailer suspension, brake, axle, bearing, and wiring work, as well as body repairs for campers and horse trailers. In-house fabrication produces custom flatbeds, front and rear bumpers, service bodies, headache racks, toolboxes, and accessory lighting. The team also installs liftgates, hoists, snowplows, auto-crane cranes, hitches, dump bodies, sanders, and tire holders. As a Steer In® Outpost, the company sells new trailers and stocks Dexter Axle components.

Customers include commercial trucking fleets, agricultural operators, construction firms, and recreational vehicle owners throughout northwestern Montana. The shop works on all makes of trucks and trailers, from light-duty pickups to heavy commercial units.

Pierce Manufacturing emphasizes competitive pricing, honest dealing, and on-time delivery as the foundation of its reputation. The company states that it holds itself to the same standard of excellence established at its founding, aiming to return every truck and trailer to working condition quickly.

about:
Pine Electronics, Inc. operates from Grove City, Pennsylvania, at the intersection of Interstates 79 and 80. The company serves as an electronics and electromechanical assembly contract manufacturer for industrial equipment OEMs across the United States.

The firm specializes in low- to mid-volume production, offering through-hole and surface-mount PCB assembly, cable and wire harness fabrication, box build integration, and full electromechanical assembly. A collective workforce of more than 100 employees supports these services from a facility the company describes as state-of-the-art.

Pine's customer base spans mass transit, mining, electrical transmission, rail, and communications sectors, serving both multinational corporations and regional businesses. Each client is assigned a dedicated representative to handle commercial and technical inquiries, a model intended to streamline communication and accelerate project development.

Quality assurance is anchored by an ISO 9001:2015 certified system, with IPC-certified trainers on staff for IPC-A-610 and IPC/WHMA-A-620 standards. An auditor noted the company's proprietary ERP software, which optimizes cycle counting for high-usage or problematic parts, as an innovative feature for a company of its size.

name: Pioneer Automotive Industries LLC
old_description: Since 1946, Pioneer Automotive Industries has been dedicated to delivering high-quality automotive components with precision and reliability. Our commitment to innovation, engineering excellence, and customer satisfaction has made us a trusted partner across the Americas.
about:
Pioneer Automotive Industries was founded in 1946 by Herman A. Shields in Meridian, Mississippi. The company began as a manufacturer of engine and transmission components. Over the decades it changed hands several times: acquired by The Barnes Group in 1979, then by UIS Inc. in 1993, then by United Components (part of The Carlyle Group) in 2003, then ownership transitioned to Doron Arad in 2006, and later joined The Lodi Group in 2009–2010. In 2017 it acquired ATP Automotive and expanded its Meridian facility to 300,000 square feet in 2018.

Today Pioneer operates a 300,000 sq ft manufacturing and distribution facility in Meridian, producing over 15,000 SKUs of powertrain and transmission components. Its product lines include flexplates, flywheels, automatic and manual transmission shift cables, clutch cables, speedometer cables, engine mounts, harmonic balancers, and a range of high‑performance parts. The company designs, manufactures, and distributes these components for the automotive aftermarket.

Pioneer serves customers and distributors throughout the United States, Canada, and Latin America. Its primary market is the global automotive aftermarket, supplying repair shops, warehouse distributors, and retail chains with replacement parts for passenger cars and light trucks.

The company states its mission is to deliver reliability, precision, and value through engineering expertise and operational excellence, aiming to be recognized as a North American brand in the automotive industry.

name: Plastic Design & Manufacturing
old_description: PDM was founded in 1998 as a full-service consulting company developing turn key manufacturing programs for the sporting, industrial, and automotive markets.  The success of these programs led to the creation of our factory direct sourcing for tooling and eventually plastic parts and assemblies from our custom built factory in 2009 located in beautiful southwest Montana.  Our growth continues with molding operations in Juarez Mexico, and Shenzhen China for production tooling and sourcing.
about:
Plastic Design & Manufacturing (PDM Plastics) was founded in 1998 in Manhattan, Montana, as a full-service consulting firm developing turnkey manufacturing programs for the sporting, industrial, and automotive markets. The company transitioned to direct manufacturing in 2009 with a custom-built factory in southwest Montana, and later expanded to molding operations in Juárez, Mexico, and Shenzhen, China, for production tooling and sourcing.

Today PDM operates two primary production plants—its headquarters in Manhattan, Montana, and a facility in Juárez, Mexico—running 22 injection molding machines ranging from 50 to 1,400 tons. The company provides custom injection molding, tooling design and build, assembly, packaging, decoration, design assistance, prototyping, and secondary operations, serving high- to medium-volume plastic component needs.

PDM serves a diverse industrial base including automotive, electronics, medical, industrial equipment, sporting goods and firearms, pet products, agricultural, construction, consumer goods, and battery components. Customers range from OEMs requiring safety-critical automotive parts to brands seeking consumer-grade plastic assemblies.

The company emphasizes low-overhead, non-union facilities operating 24 hours a day, five to seven days a week, with global sourcing capabilities. It highlights value engineering, contract pricing on materials, and a preference for recycled and bio-based resins where applicable, alongside environmentally sound manufacturing practices.

name: Plastic Design Company
old_description: PDC is a USA based market leader in precision injection molding and value-added assembly, partnering with OEMs and contract manufacturers worldwide to deliver molded and micro-molded solutions for medical devices, diagnostics, and biotechnology applications. Our vertically integrated facility specializes in in-house tool design and mold fabrication for injection molding high-performance thermoplastics, including PEEK, Cyclic Olefin Copolymer (COC), Cyclic Olefin Polymer (COP), and PEBA. We also can customize material blends with colorants and functional additives.
about:
Plastic Design Company (PDC) is based in Scottsdale, Arizona, where it operates a vertically integrated facility specializing in precision injection molding and micro-molding for medical device, diagnostics, and biotechnology applications. The company partners with OEMs and contract manufacturers worldwide.

PDC provides precision injection molding, micro-molding, insert molding, and over-molding services, supported by in-house tool design and mold fabrication. All production takes place in an ISO 8 cleanroom equipped with automated machinery. The company works with high-performance thermoplastics such as PEEK, COC, COP, PEBA, polycarbonate, PMMA, and polystyrene, and can customize material blends with colorants and functional additives. Its capabilities span from design and development through high-volume production, including value-added assembly, measurement, inspection, and program management.

The company serves medical device OEMs and contract manufacturers across segments including diagnostics, drug delivery, orthopedic sports medicine, proteomics and genomics, robotic assisted surgery, and vascular surgery. Typical components produced include multi-part diagnostic cartridge housings with molded-in alignment features, surgical instrument assemblies with rod-based actuation components, implantable or wearable components with over-molded metal contacts, capillary components, lateral flow assay components, optical components, valve components, and cannula assemblies.

PDC emphasizes its vertically integrated model, noting that in-house tooling gives it control over iterations and scheduling, while its cleanroom environment and material expertise enable quick decision-making and flexibility for complex medical applications.
